examples.ko: 우리 학교 학칙에 따르면 교실에서 모자를 쓰면 안 돼요.
examples.en: According to our school regulations, you can't wear a hat in the classroom.

examples.ko: 학칙을 어기면 선생님께 주의를 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you break the school regulations, a teacher may warn you.

examples.ko: 이번에 학칙이 바뀌어서 지각 규정이 더 엄격해졌어요.
examples.en: The school regulations changed this time, and the rules on being late became stricter.

examples.ko: 휴대폰 사용 시간은 학칙으로 정해져 있어요.
examples.en: The hours you may use your phone are set by the school regulations.

examples.ko: 학칙은 학교 홈페이지에서 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can read the school regulations on the school website.

examples.ko: 입학하기 전에 학칙을 꼼꼼히 읽어 보세요.
examples.en: Please read the school regulations carefully before you enroll.

explain: 학교가 문서로 정해 둔 운영 규칙을 말해요. '교칙'도 비슷하게 쓰이고, 학생이 지켜야 할 생활 규칙은 '교칙'이라고도 많이 말해요. 보통 '학칙에 따라', '학칙을 어기다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the operating rules a school has put in writing. '교칙' is used in a similar way, and rules for student conduct are often called '교칙' too. It usually appears in patterns like '학칙에 따라' (according to the regulations) and '학칙을 어기다' (break the regulations).

examples.en: This university is famous for its free academic atmosphere.

examples.ko: 학교마다 학풍이 달라서 선택할 때 고민이 돼요.
examples.en: Each school has a different academic tradition, so choosing is hard.
That professor dislikes a conservative academic tradition.

examples.ko: 우리 학과의 학풍은 토론을 중요하게 생각해요.
examples.en: The academic culture of our department values discussion.

examples.ko: 저는 이 학교의 학풍에 잘 맞는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think I fit well with this school's academic culture.

examples.ko: 새 총장님이 오신 뒤로 학풍도 많이 달라졌어요.
examples.en: Since the new president came, the academic culture has changed a lot too.

explain: 학교나 학파가 오래 가지고 있는 공부 분위기와 전통을 말해요. 주로 대학이나 연구 이야기에서 쓰고, 가볍게는 '학교 분위기'라고 말하기도 해요. '자유로운 학풍', '보수적인 학풍'처럼 꾸미는 말과 자주 함께 나와요.
explain_en: It means the study atmosphere and tradition that a school or academic group has kept for a long time. It is mostly used about universities and research, and in casual talk people may say '학교 분위기' instead. It often appears with describing words, as in '자유로운 학풍' (a free academic culture) or '보수적인 학풍' (a conservative one).

en: being masterful; being great; being famous; being leading

examples.ko: 우리 할아버지는 젊었을 때 노래로 한가락 하셨대요.
examples.en: They say my grandfather was quite a singer when he was young.

examples.ko: 저 친구도 농구라면 한가락 하는 것 같아요.
examples.en: That friend seems to be pretty good at basketball too.
When it comes to cooking, I'm pretty good too.

examples.ko: 이 동네에서 한가락 하는 분들이 다 모였어요.
examples.en: All the big names of this neighborhood have gathered.

examples.ko: 그분은 왕년에 야구로 한가락 하던 선수예요.
examples.en: He is a player who was a big name in baseball in his day.

examples.ko: 한가락 한다는 사람들 사이에서도 그 친구는 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: Even among people who are known to be good, that friend stands out.

explain: 거의 '한가락 하다' 꼴로만 써요. 어떤 분야에서 실력이나 이름이 상당하다고 인정할 때 쓰는 편한 말투예요. 비슷한 말로 '한 실력 하다'도 있어요.
explain_en: It is almost always used in the form '한가락 하다'. It is a casual way to say someone is recognized as quite skilled or well known in some field. '한 실력 하다' is a similar expression.

examples.en: On the weekend afternoon I took a leisurely walk in the park.

examples.ko: 호수 위에 오리들이 한가로이 떠 있어요.
examples.en: Ducks are floating leisurely on the lake.

examples.ko: 요즘은 한가로이 커피 마실 시간도 없어요.
examples.en: These days I don't even have time to drink coffee at leisure.

examples.ko: 시골에서는 소들이 한가로이 풀을 뜯고 있어요.
examples.en: In the countryside, cows are grazing peacefully.

examples.ko: 휴가 때는 한가로이 책이나 읽고 싶어요.
examples.en: On vacation I'd like to just read a book at my leisure.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 마루에 앉아 한가로이 바둑을 두세요.
examples.en: Grandfather sits on the porch and plays baduk at a relaxed pace.

explain: '한가하게'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 '한가로이'는 풍경이나 분위기를 그릴 때 더 잘 어울려요. 바쁜 일 없이 느긋한 모습에 쓰고, 반대 느낌의 말은 '바삐'예요. 대화보다 글에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is close to '한가하게', but '한가로이' fits better when describing a scene or mood. It describes a relaxed manner with nothing urgent to do, and its opposite is '바삐' (in a hurry). You see it more in writing than in conversation.

en: quiet and leisurely; unhurried and restful

examples.en: There is a small cafe in a quiet alley.

examples.ko: 평일 낮의 도서관은 한갓져서 공부하기 좋아요.
examples.en: The library on weekday afternoons is quiet and relaxed, so it's good for studying.

examples.ko: 사람이 없는 시간에 가면 한갓지게 구경할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you go when there are few people, you can look around at ease.

examples.ko: 시끄러운 도시를 떠나 한갓진 시골에서 살고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to leave the noisy city and live in a peaceful countryside.
There are no customers today, so the shop is quiet and relaxed.

examples.ko: 한갓지지 않은 시간에는 이 길이 아주 복잡해요.
examples.en: At busy times, this road is very crowded.

explain: '한적하다'와 비슷하게 사람이 적고 느긋한 장소나 시간에 써요. '한갓져요', '한갓진'으로 활용해요. 일상에서는 '한가하다'나 '조용하다'를 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Like '한적하다', it is used for a place or time with few people and a relaxed feel. It conjugates as '한갓져요' and '한갓진'. In everyday talk, people more often say '한가하다' or '조용하다'.

examples.en: My friend and I were born on the same day at the same time.
We are colleagues who joined the company on the very same day.
The brothers held their weddings on the same day and at the same time.

examples.ko: 그 두 회사가 한날한시에 신제품을 발표했어요.
examples.en: Those two companies announced new products at exactly the same time.
It happened at the very same time, so it's really a coincidence.
The friends who gathered on the same day laughed together for the first time in a while.

explain: 거의 '한날한시에' 꼴로 써서 같은 날 같은 시각에 일이 겹친 것을 강조해요. 우연이라서 놀랍거나 일부러 맞췄다는 느낌을 줄 때 좋아요. 그냥 '같은 날'보다 더 딱 맞는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is almost always used as '한날한시에' to stress that things happened on the same day at the same moment. It works well for a surprising coincidence or for something deliberately timed together. It feels more exact than simply saying '같은 날' (the same day).

examples.ko: 할머니들이 마루에 모여 한담을 나누고 있어요.
examples.en: The grandmothers are gathered on the porch chatting.
The small talk went on so long that the meeting started late.
I just dropped by for a little chat.
We passed the time chatting over tea.
The two people's chat continued until late at night.
Let's put work aside and start with some small talk.

explain: 일상에서는 '수다'나 '잡담'을 더 많이 말하고, '한담'은 점잖고 글 같은 느낌이에요. 급하지 않고 한가롭게 나누는 가벼운 이야기에 어울려요. '한담을 나누다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: In daily talk people more often say '수다' or '잡담', while '한담' sounds polite and a bit literary. It suits light, unhurried conversation with no urgency. It is often used as '한담을 나누다' (to have a chat).

examples.en: I spent time chatting with a friend at a cafe.
After work I sometimes chat with my coworkers.
The grandfathers are sitting on the bench platform chatting.

examples.ko: 한담할 시간이 있으면 같이 차 한잔해요.
examples.en: If you have time to chat, let's have a cup of tea together.
Yesterday I chatted with my neighbor for quite a while.
Please don't chat for long when we are busy.

explain: 말할 때는 '이야기하다', '수다 떨다'가 더 자연스럽고, '한담하다'는 글이나 점잖은 말투에서 보여요. 한가롭게 가벼운 이야기를 나눈다는 느낌이에요. 보통 '~와/과 한담하다'로 써요.
explain_en: In speech, '이야기하다' or '수다 떨다' sounds more natural, while '한담하다' appears in writing or polite speech. It gives a feel of having a light, relaxed talk. It is usually used as '~와/과 한담하다' (chat with someone).

examples.en: I want to raise my card limit.

examples.ko: 이번 달 한도액이 거의 다 찼어요.
examples.en: I've almost used up this month's limit.
The daily transfer limit differs from bank to bank.
If you spend up to the limit, next month will be hard.

examples.ko: 보험 한도액 안에서 치료비를 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can receive treatment costs within the insurance limit.

examples.ko: 한도액에 비해 사용 금액이 너무 많아요.
examples.en: The amount used is too high compared to the limit.

explain: 돈의 액수에서 넘으면 안 되는 위쪽 끝을 말해요. 카드, 대출, 이체, 보험처럼 금융 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 말할 때는 '한도'만 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the upper end of a money amount that must not be exceeded. It often appears in finance topics such as cards, loans, transfers and insurance. In speech, people sometimes say just '한도'.

examples.en: The cosmos flowers sway in the wind.
The curtain swaying by the window looks pretty.
The petal fluttered for a while and then fell to the ground.
The willow branches swayed in the spring breeze.
The wind chime swayed and made a clear sound.
The laundry swayed in the wind and dried quickly.

explain: 가벼운 것이 바람에 부드럽게 흔들리는 모습에 써요. '흔들리다'보다 가볍고 예쁜 느낌이고, 비슷한 말로 '한들대다', '살랑거리다'가 있어요. 꽃, 풀, 커튼 같은 가벼운 것에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It describes light things swaying softly in the wind. It feels lighter and prettier than '흔들리다', and '한들대다' and '살랑거리다' are similar. It suits light things like flowers, grass and curtains.

examples.en: The cosmos flowers sway gently in the wind.
The laundry is fluttering gently.
The balloon moves back and forth at the end of the string.
The gently swaying reeds are really pretty.

examples.ko: 커튼이 한들한들 움직이니 바람이 오나 봐요.
examples.en: The curtain is swaying, so I guess a breeze is coming.
The child waved a hand lightly and said hello.

explain: 가볍고 부드러운 것이 천천히 흔들리는 모습을 흉내 낸 말이에요. '살랑살랑', '하늘하늘'과 느낌이 비슷하지만, 바람에 계속 흔들리는 장면에 특히 잘 어울려요. 동사는 '한들거리다'를 써요.
explain_en: It imitates the look of something light and soft swaying slowly. It feels close to '살랑살랑' and '하늘하늘', but fits especially well with scenes of something moving continuously in the wind. The matching verb is '한들거리다'.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 일은 안 하고 놀기만 하는 한량이에요.
examples.en: That man is a loafer who only plays and doesn't work.

examples.ko: 젊은 시절 우리 삼촌은 한량 소리를 들었대요.
examples.en: They say my uncle was called a playboy in his youth.
Many of my friends say they want to live like a carefree gentleman.
Her husband is a loafer, so his wife has a hard time.
He who had been living as a loafer finally got a job.

examples.ko: 저는 한량 기질이 있어서 회사 생활이 안 맞아요.
examples.en: I have a loafer's temperament, so office life doesn't suit me.

explain: 일은 많이 안 하고 놀러 다니며 한가롭게 지내는 사람을 가리켜요. 놀리거나 비꼬는 말투로 쓰는 일이 많지만, 약간 부러워하는 느낌으로도 말해요. '백수'는 일자리가 없는 상태를 말하고, '한량'은 놀기 좋아하고 멋 부리는 성격에 가까워요.
explain_en: It refers to a person who does little work and spends time leisurely, going out and having fun. It is often used teasingly or sarcastically, but sometimes with a touch of envy. '백수' describes being without a job, while '한량' is closer to a fun-loving, stylish personality.

en: play a role; play a part

examples.en: That song played a part in the drama's popularity.
The good weather also plays a role in the festival's success.

examples.ko: 친구의 응원이 합격에 한몫한 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think my friend's encouragement helped me pass.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 편리해서 인기를 얻는 데 한몫하고 있어요.
examples.en: This app is convenient, which is helping it become popular.

examples.ko: 가격이 싼 것도 한몫하겠지만 품질이 더 중요해요.
examples.en: The low price will play a part too, but quality is more important.

examples.ko: 당신도 이번 일에 한몫했으니 같이 축하해요.
examples.en: You played a part in this too, so let's celebrate together.

explain: 'N이/가 ~에 한몫하다'처럼 어떤 일에 도움이 되거나 영향을 준 몫이 크다고 말할 때 써요. 좋은 결과에 많이 쓰지만 나쁜 결과에도 쓸 수 있어요. '한몫 잡다'처럼 큰 이익을 얻는 뜻의 표현과는 쓰임이 달라요.
explain_en: It is used as 'N이/가 ~에 한몫하다' to say something contributed a good share to a result. It is often used for good outcomes but can also be used for bad ones. It is different from '한몫 잡다', which means making a big profit.

en: be out of season; be past one's prime

examples.en: These days that trend is already past its peak.
Even if the song is past its prime, I still like it.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 한물갔다는 소리를 들었지만 다시 인기를 얻었어요.
examples.en: That singer was said to be washed up but became popular again.
The fish is past its best, so it doesn't taste good.
These days this style is going out of fashion.
Buy it quickly before it goes out of season.

explain: 과일이나 생선은 제철이 지났을 때, 유행이나 사람은 인기와 전성기가 지났을 때 써요. 사람에게 '한물갔다'고 하면 무례하게 들릴 수 있으니 조심하세요. 반대 느낌으로는 '한창이다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used when fruit or fish is past its season, or when a trend or a person is past peak popularity. Saying a person has '한물갔다' can sound rude, so be careful. The opposite feeling is expressed with '한창이다' (to be at its peak).

examples.en: They say he made a fortune from his business.

examples.ko: 한밑천 마련해서 작은 가게를 열고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to raise a good sum and open a small shop.

examples.ko: 아버지가 물려주신 땅이 우리 집의 한밑천이었어요.
examples.en: The land my father left us was our family's nest egg.
I'm working hard to save up a good sum.

examples.ko: 이번 사업으로 한밑천 챙기려는 사람들이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people are trying to make a big profit from this business.
A large sum went into the children's education.

explain: '밑천'은 장사나 일을 시작할 때 쓰는 돈인데, '한밑천'은 그중 꽤 큰 돈을 말해요. '한밑천 잡다', '한밑천 마련하다', '한밑천 들다'처럼 짝지어 써요. 편한 대화에서 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: '밑천' is the money used to start a business or venture, and '한밑천' means a fairly large sum of it. It pairs with verbs as in '한밑천 잡다' (make a fortune), '한밑천 마련하다' (raise a good sum) and '한밑천 들다' (cost a lot). It is a casual, conversational word.

examples.ko: 한세상 사는 거 너무 걱정하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't worry too much about living your life.
I want to live a happy life and then go.

examples.ko: 우리 할머니는 한세상을 농사만 지으며 사셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother spent her whole life only farming.
A whole lifetime passed in the blink of an eye.
We promised to live our lives together.

examples.ko: 인생 한세상 뭐 그리 대단한 게 있나요?
examples.en: What is so great about a single lifetime, really?

explain: '평생', '일생'과 비슷하지만 '한세상 살다'처럼 인생을 담담하게, 때로는 허무하게 돌아볼 때 어울려요. '인생 한세상'이라는 말투로 많이 써요. 격식 있는 글보다 이야기하듯 하는 말에 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is close to '평생' and '일생', but it fits when looking back on life calmly, sometimes with a sense of emptiness, as in '한세상 살다'. It is often used in the phrase '인생 한세상'. It sounds more natural in storytelling talk than in formal writing.

en: eating from the same pot; sharing the same table

examples.ko: 우리는 한솥밥을 먹던 사이라서 정이 깊어요.
examples.en: We used to live and eat together, so our bond is deep.
They are coworkers who have worked together for a long time.

examples.ko: 한솥밥 먹는 식구끼리 왜 이렇게 싸워요?
examples.en: Why do family members who share the same table fight like this?

examples.ko: 군대에서 한솥밥 먹은 친구를 오랜만에 만났어요.
examples.en: I met a friend I shared army life with after a long time.

examples.ko: 같은 팀에서 한솥밥을 먹다가 다른 회사로 옮겼어요.
examples.en: After working on the same team for a while, I moved to another company.

examples.ko: 한솥밥 먹던 정을 생각해서 이번에는 봐 줄게요.
examples.en: Thinking of our time together, I'll let it go this time.

explain: 가족, 학교, 회사, 군대처럼 오래 같이 지낸 사이를 가리켜요. '동료'보다 함께 먹고 생활하며 쌓인 정이 느껴져요. 헤어진 뒤에도 '한솥밥 먹던 사이'라고 하고, 보통 '한솥밥을 먹다' 꼴로 말해요.

phrases.example: 우리는 십 년 동안 한솥밥을 먹은 사이예요.
phrases.en: to live or work together in the same group and become close
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 같은 밥을 먹는다는 뜻보다 같은 집단에서 함께 지낸 정을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is less about literally eating the same rice and more about the bond from belonging to the same group.
phrases.en_equiv: to share the same table; to live and work side by side

explain_en: It refers to people who have spent a long time together, such as family, school, work or the military. Compared with '동료' (colleague), it carries the closeness built by living and eating together. People say '한솥밥 먹던 사이' even after parting, and it is usually used as '한솥밥을 먹다'.

en: a little; a bit; one spoonful; one bite

examples.ko: 입맛이 없어서 밥을 한술도 못 떴어요.
examples.en: I had no appetite and couldn't eat even one spoonful of rice.

examples.ko: 한술 더 떠서 이제는 거짓말까지 해요.
examples.en: He's gone one step further and now even tells lies.
I know you're busy, but have a bite before you go.

examples.ko: 아파서 못 먹는다면 죽을 한술씩 천천히 드세요.
examples.en: If you're too sick to eat, take the porridge slowly, a spoonful at a time.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 나보다 한술 더 뜨는 장난꾸러기예요.
examples.en: That friend is an even bigger prankster than me.
Please have at least a spoonful of porridge in the morning before you go.

explain: 숟가락으로 한 번 뜬 만큼의 적은 양이에요. 입맛이 없을 때 '한술도 못 뜨다'처럼 부정과 함께 자주 쓰고, '한술 더 뜨다'는 어떤 면에서 더 심하다는 뜻으로 써요. 보통 밥, 죽, 국에 말해요.

phrases.example: 동생은 나보다 한술 더 떠서 늘 늦게 와요.
phrases.en: to go even further than someone else, usually in a bad way
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대보다 정도가 더 심할 때 쓰며 보통 부정적인 상황이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone goes beyond another person's level, usually in a negative situation.
phrases.en_equiv: to go one better; to top someone

explain_en: It is the small amount you get with one scoop of a spoon. It is often used with negatives like '한술도 못 뜨다' when you have no appetite, and '한술 더 뜨다' means to go even further in some way. It is mostly said of rice, porridge or soup.

examples.en: The child sighed after seeing the report card.
My father sighed while looking out the window.
Don't just sigh, let's look for a way together.
Many people sigh because payday is far away.
She shook her head with a sigh.
I often sigh over rising prices.

explain: 걱정이나 실망 때문에 크게 숨을 내쉬는 것으로, 대화에서는 '한숨을 쉬다'가 더 자연스러워요. '한숨짓다'는 글이나 이야기 속 표현에서 많이 보여요. 'ㅅ' 불규칙이라 '한숨지어요', '한숨지으며'로 활용해요.
explain_en: It means to breathe out heavily from worry or disappointment, and in conversation '한숨을 쉬다' is more natural. '한숨짓다' shows up more in writing and storytelling. It is a ㅅ-irregular verb, so it becomes '한숨지어요' and '한숨지으며'.

examples.en: The exam is over, so I can finally relax.

examples.ko: 한시름 덜었으니 이제 좀 쉬어도 돼요.
examples.en: Now that one worry is off my mind, I can rest a bit.
Thank you for taking a big worry off my mind.
Their son got a job, so his parents could set their minds at ease.

examples.ko: 대출을 다 갚으니 한시름이 사라진 기분이에요.
examples.en: After paying off the loan, I feel a big worry has disappeared.

examples.ko: 이제 한시름 놓았다고 방심하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't let your guard down just because you're relieved now.

explain: 큰 걱정 하나를 가리키며, 거의 '한시름 놓다', '한시름 덜다'처럼 써요. 걱정거리가 해결되어 마음이 놓일 때 써서 안도하는 느낌이 있어요. 놓다·덜다 말고 다른 동사와는 잘 안 써요.

phrases.en: to feel relieved because a big worry is gone
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정거리가 해결되어 마음이 편해졌을 때 쓰는 굳은 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A fixed expression used when a worry is resolved and you can relax.
phrases.en_equiv: to breathe a sigh of relief

explain_en: It points to one big worry and is almost always used as '한시름 놓다' or '한시름 덜다'. It carries a feeling of relief when a concern has been resolved. It is rarely combined with verbs other than 놓다 and 덜다.

en: as soon as possible; hurriedly; quickly

examples.ko: 열이 많이 나니까 한시바삐 병원에 가 보세요.
examples.en: You have a high fever, so please go to the hospital as soon as you can.
I want to go home and rest as soon as possible.

examples.ko: 아이는 한시바삐 엄마를 만나고 싶어 했어요.
examples.en: The child wanted to see his mom as quickly as possible.
We have to finish this work as soon as possible.
Hearing the news, he rushed over without delay.

examples.ko: 한시바삐 사과하는 게 좋을 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think it's better to apologize as soon as possible.

explain: '빨리', '하루빨리'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 한 시각도 미루기 어려운 급한 마음이 들어 있어요. 말보다는 글이나 조금 격식 있는 말투에서 자주 보여요. 뒤에는 '~고 싶다', '~야 하다'처럼 바람이나 필요를 말하는 표현이 자주 와요.
explain_en: It is similar to '빨리' and '하루빨리', but it carries an urgent feeling that even an hour of delay is hard. You see it more in writing or somewhat formal speech. It is often followed by wishes or needs, such as '~고 싶다' or '~야 하다'.

examples.ko: 이 할인은 한시적 행사라서 이번 주까지만 해요.
examples.en: This discount is a limited-time event, so it runs only until this week.
The government decided to give a temporary subsidy.

examples.ko: 한시적 조치였지만 효과가 커서 계속하기로 했어요.
examples.en: It was a temporary measure, but it worked so well that they decided to continue.
The company started temporary remote work.

examples.ko: 한시적 계약이라 내년에는 일자리를 다시 찾아야 해요.
examples.en: It's a fixed-term contract, so I have to look for a job again next year.
That road is a temporarily closed section.

explain: 정해진 기간 동안만 한다는 뜻으로, 제도, 정책, 행사, 계약 같은 이야기에서 자주 써요. '일시적'은 잠깐 생겼다 사라지는 상태에 쓰고, '한시적'은 기간이 미리 정해진 경우에 잘 어울려요. '한시적으로 운영하다'처럼 부사 꼴도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It means something lasts only for a set period, and it is common with systems, policies, events and contracts. '일시적' fits a state that appears briefly and fades, while '한시적' fits cases where the period is set in advance. The adverb form is also common, as in '한시적으로 운영하다' (operate for a limited time).

examples.en: The love my parents gave me is truly boundless.
I don't know how to repay my endless gratitude.
I was endlessly happy when I heard I passed.
She comforted the child with an infinitely gentle voice.

examples.ko: 그 말을 들으니 제 자신이 한없이 작아졌어요.
examples.en: Hearing those words, I felt infinitely small.

examples.ko: 한없던 슬픔도 시간이 지나니 조금씩 줄었어요.
examples.en: Even my endless sadness slowly lessened as time passed.

explain: '끝없다'는 길, 바다처럼 눈에 보이는 것에도 많이 쓰고, '한없다'는 사랑, 기쁨, 슬픔 같은 마음에 자주 써요. 대부분 '한없이' 꼴로 나오고, '한없는 사랑'처럼 꾸밀 때는 '한없는'을 써요.
explain_en: '끝없다' is often used for visible things like roads or the sea, while '한없다' is often used for feelings such as love, joy and sadness. It mostly appears as '한없이', and '한없는' is used to modify a noun, as in '한없는 사랑' (boundless love).

examples.ko: 이 약은 한정적 효과만 있어서 치료를 따로 받아야 해요.
examples.en: This medicine has only a limited effect, so you need to get treatment separately.

examples.ko: 한정적 자원으로 최대한 좋은 결과를 내야 해요.
examples.en: We have to get the best possible result with limited resources.
That rule applies only in limited situations.

examples.ko: 한정적 의미로만 이해하면 글이 잘못 읽힐 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you understand it only in a narrow sense, the text can be misread.
My experience is limited, so it's hard to generalize.

examples.ko: 이 서비스는 한정적 지역에서만 이용할 수 있어요.
examples.en: This service can only be used in limited areas.

explain: 범위나 수량이 어느 한도 안으로 정해져 있다는 뜻으로 써요. '제한적'과 비슷하지만 '한정적'은 범위가 좁게 정해진 느낌이 강해요. 뒤에 명사가 오거나 '한정적이다' 꼴로 쓰고, 글이나 설명에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It says that a range or amount is fixed within some limit. It is similar to '제한적', but '한정적' stresses that the range is narrowly set. It goes before a noun or appears as '한정적이다', and is common in writing and explanations.

en: days of one's youth; prime; bloom

examples.ko: 한창나이에 건강을 조심하지 않으면 나중에 후회해요.
examples.en: If you don't take care of your health in your prime, you'll regret it later.
You're still in your prime, and you want to retire already?
Young people in their prime are looking for jobs.
I spent my prime years only on studying.

examples.ko: 한창나이라 그런지 먹어도 금방 배가 고파요.
examples.en: Maybe because I'm in my prime, I get hungry quickly even after eating.

examples.ko: 한창나이에는 밤을 새워도 괜찮았는데 이제는 힘들어요.
examples.en: In my prime I was fine staying up all night, but now it's hard.

explain: 힘이 넘치고 가장 활발한 젊은 시절을 가리켜요. '한창때'와 거의 같지만 '나이'가 들어가서 나이를 강조하는 느낌이에요. 아쉬움이나 안타까움을 말할 때도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the youthful years when you are full of energy and most active. It is almost the same as '한창때', but the word '나이' (age) gives it more focus on age. It is often used when expressing regret or sympathy as well.

examples.en: My father played as a football player in his prime.

examples.ko: 한창때는 하루에 열 시간씩 일해도 괜찮았어요.
examples.en: In my prime I was fine working ten hours a day.

examples.ko: 지금은 한창때가 지나서 체력이 많이 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: My prime has passed, so my stamina has dropped a lot.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 한창때의 인기를 되찾고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: That singer wants to regain the popularity of her peak.

examples.ko: 한창때에는 밤새 놀아도 다음 날 멀쩡했어요.
examples.en: In my prime I could play all night and still be fine the next day.

examples.ko: 한창때를 지난 선수에게 너무 많은 걸 기대하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't expect too much from a player past his prime.

explain: 가장 힘이 왕성하고 활발한 시기를 말해요. 사람뿐 아니라 계절이나 일의 가장 바쁜 때에도 써요. '한창이다'는 지금 한창 진행 중이라는 말이라서 '공사가 한창이에요'처럼 달라요.
explain_en: It means the time when strength and activity are at their greatest. It is used not only for people but also for the peak of a season or the busiest time of a task. '한창이다' is different: it means something is in full swing now, as in '공사가 한창이에요' (construction is in full swing).

examples.en: If you get caught up in a get-rich-quick mindset and invest recklessly, it's dangerous.
You should drop the get-rich-quick mindset and work honestly.
I'm worried that a get-rich-quick mentality is spreading in society.
A get-rich-quick mindset ends up ruining people.

examples.ko: 젊은이들 사이의 한탕주의 때문에 사기 피해가 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: Fraud damage is increasing because of the get-rich-quick mindset among young people.

examples.ko: 그는 한탕주의적 생각 때문에 계속 실패했어요.
examples.en: He kept failing because of his get-rich-quick thinking.

explain: 힘들이지 않고 단번에 큰돈을 벌려는 생각을 비판할 때 써요. 한자어 '일확천금'과 뜻이 가깝지만, '한탕주의'는 그런 태도나 사회 분위기를 말해요. 뉴스나 칼럼에서 자주 나오고, 좋은 뜻으로는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is used to criticize the idea of making a lot of money at once without effort. It is close to '일확천금' (a sudden fortune), but '한탕주의' refers to that attitude or social mood. It often appears in news and columns and is never used positively.

examples.en: There is a rumor that the two of them are in cahoots.

examples.ko: 너도 걔네랑 한통속이지요? 솔직히 말해 줘요.
examples.en: You're in on it with them too, aren't you? Tell me honestly.

examples.ko: 그 가게와 업자가 한통속이 되어 가격을 올렸어요.
examples.en: That shop and the dealer teamed up and raised the price.
We're in this together, so let's take responsibility together.
I'm even accused of being in on it, and it's so unfair.
Your words are exactly the same, as if you were in cahoots.

explain: 주로 좋지 않은 일을 같이 꾸미는 같은 편이라는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 중립적으로 '같은 편'이라고 할 때는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요. 비슷한 말로 '한패'가 있어요.
explain_en: It usually carries a negative feel of people on the same side in doing something bad together. It is best not to use it for a neutral 'same team'. '한패' is a similar word.

en: a notch; somewhat; a bit of one's edge

examples.en: After the rainy season passed, the heat let up a bit.

examples.ko: 기세가 한풀 꺾인 팀은 후반에 무너졌어요.
examples.en: The team that lost some of its momentum collapsed in the second half.

examples.ko: 감기 증상이 이제 한풀 꺾인 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think my cold symptoms have eased up now.

examples.ko: 인기가 한풀 꺾이더니 요즘은 보기 어려워요.
examples.en: Its popularity cooled off, and now it's hard to see.
When the shower came, the heat eased off a bit too.

examples.ko: 비판이 쏟아지자 그의 자신감이 한풀 꺾였어요.
examples.en: When criticism poured in, his confidence took a hit.

explain: 거의 '한풀 꺾이다' 꼴로 써서 더위, 기세, 인기처럼 세던 것이 조금 약해졌다는 뜻을 나타내요. 아주 없어진 것이 아니라 한 단계 누그러진 느낌이에요. 반대로 더위가 심할 때는 '기승을 부리다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is almost always used as '한풀 꺾이다' to show that something strong, like heat, momentum or popularity, has weakened a bit. It does not mean gone completely, just eased by a notch. The opposite, when heat is severe, is expressed with '기승을 부리다'.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 지난 대회의 한풀이를 하겠다고 말했어요.
examples.en: That player said he would make up for last tournament's disappointment.
To make up for my long frustration, I'll eat as much as I want today.

examples.ko: 오랜 설움의 한풀이라고 생각하니 마음이 아파요.
examples.en: It hurts to think of it as the release of long-held sorrow.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 억울하게 진 사람의 한풀이 이야기예요.
examples.en: That movie is a story of someone wronged finally getting release for their grief.

examples.ko: 이번 승리는 지난해 패배에 대한 한풀이예요.
examples.en: This victory is payback for last year's defeat.
The scene of the dance releasing deep sorrow was impressive.

explain: '한(恨)'은 오래 쌓인 억울함과 응어리인데, 한풀이는 그것을 푸는 것을 말해요. '화풀이'는 화가 난 감정을 푸는 것이고, 한풀이는 오래 쌓인 아쉬움을 푸는 것이라 더 깊은 느낌이에요. 복수의 뜻으로 쓰일 때도 있어요.
explain_en: '한(恨)' is long-built-up resentment and sorrow, and '한풀이' means releasing it. '화풀이' is venting anger, while '한풀이' is releasing a long-held regret, so it feels deeper. It can sometimes also mean revenge.
